title: Ibrahim bin al-Mahdi and the Barber-Surgeon (मराठी)

keywords: ibrahim bin al-mahdi and the barber-surgeon
full_text:
Prince Ibrahim bin al-Mahdi, uncle of the Caliph Al-Ma'mun, was a man of royal blood and celebrated musical genius. Following a bitter political rebellion in Baghdad, Ibrahim's faction was defeated, and the Caliph put a reward of one hundred thousand gold dinars upon his uncle’s head, dead or alive.

Disguised in a tattered woollen mantle, Prince Ibrahim wandered the alleys of Baghdad, pursued by royal guards. Exhausted and desperate, he slipped into a modest mud-brick house and threw himself before the master, an impoverished barber-surgeon named Abu Ahmad.

'I am a man fleeing for my life,' gasped Ibrahim. 'If the guards find me, I perish. Protect me for the sake of ancient honor!'

Abu Ahmad asked no questions. He hid the prince in his small attic, shared his meager supper of lentils and bread, and tended his blistered feet with soothing oils.

The next morning, the town crier passed the window, proclaiming the reward of one hundred thousand dinars for Ibrahim’s capture. The barber turned to his guest with tears in his eyes: 'My lord, I recognized your noble voice last night from the days when you sang at the palace. You are worth a king's ransom, but under Abu Ahmad’s roof, a guest is worth all the gold in creation. Stay here until the storm passes.'

For three weeks, the poor barber shared his crust of bread with the royal prince. When peace was restored and the Caliph Al-Ma'mun proclaimed a universal amnesty, Ibrahim walked boldly into the imperial palace. The Caliph, moved by his uncle's poetic plea, embraced him and granted full pardon.

Ibrahim then stepped forward and said: 'Sire, I ask one favor: summon Abu Ahmad the barber.' Before the entire court, Ibrahim recounted the barber's heroic fidelity. The Caliph appointed Abu Ahmad chief physician of the royal hospital, granted him a palace on the Tigris, and decreed that true nobility is found not in crowns, but in the faithful heart of an honest man.
moral: Loyalty, hospitality to a fugitive in peril, and honorable gratitude create friendships that outlive empires. [MR]
